sections.heading: C — Accessible parking, disabilities and interstate driving
sections.markdown:
## C — Accessible parking, disabilities and interstate driving

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
West Virginia law reserves designated parking spaces for mobility impaired citizens whose condition limits their ability to walk reasonable distances, and people who routinely transport mobility impaired persons may also use those spaces [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
To obtain a mobility impaired parking placard or license plate a doctor must certify the condition on a form the DMV provides, the DMV issues the placard or plate after approving the application, and the mobility impaired license plate carries a transfer fee of ten dollars and fifty cents [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
It is illegal to park a vehicle in a designated mobility impaired area unless it displays a mobility impaired parking placard or license plate [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
About one in every ten people has some disability, no single set of rules can judge every person's ability to drive safely, and an applicant with a physical disability or medical problem that may interfere with driving should prepare a letter explaining the situation to accompany the license application [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A01
A driver who needs adaptive aids such as hand controls can get a list of manufacturers from the driver's license examiner or from the Driver Education Department of the West Virginia Division of Rehabilitation Services [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A01
Under the Americans with Disabilities Act the DMV does not discriminate on the basis of disability, generally provides aids and services for effective communication on request, makes reasonable modifications to its policies, and welcomes service animals in its offices even where pets are prohibited [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A01
Anyone who needs an auxiliary aid or a modification of DMV procedures should contact the DMV no later than forty-eight hours before the scheduled arrival [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A01
The Americans with Disabilities Act does not require the DMV to fundamentally alter its programs or take on an undue financial or administrative burden, and the DMV will not place a surcharge on a person or group with disabilities to cover the cost of aids, services or modifications [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A02
Questions or concerns about accessibility go to the DMV's ADA coordinator, and reasonable modifications include retrieving items from public locations that are not accessible to people who use wheelchairs [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A03
Interstate and divided highways have largely removed the chance of head-on collisions, but interstate driving is very different and demands complete awareness of high-speed driving and constant alertness [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A03
Trucks and buses entering an interstate may need extra time to adjust to the traffic pattern, so give them extra time and space, and slower traffic should drive in the right-hand lane except when passing [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A03
Interstate highways are identified by distinctive red, white and blue shields, even-numbered interstates run east to west, and odd-numbered interstates run north to south [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A03
A three-digit interstate number whose first digit is even identifies a beltway or bypass around a city, while a three-digit number whose first digit is odd identifies a spur route [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A03
Because interstate entrances and exits can be far apart, plan your route in advance and check gas, water, oil and tires including the spare before leaving, since a breakdown on an interstate costs time and can be dangerous [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A03
On an interstate the first guide sign for an interchange is placed well before the point where you must turn off, giving time to change lanes and exit smoothly, so watch the guide signs to avoid hazardous last-minute maneuvers [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A03
Where the number of through lanes changes, an added lane is usually obvious, while a removed lane usually ends at a fork or exit and is indicated by a black and yellow panel below the green and white overhead guide sign [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A03
An interchange is the intersection of two highways at different levels, over and under, with separate connecting roads that let vehicles cross, enter or leave either road without interfering with others, and the three most common types are cloverleaf, diamond and trumpet [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A04
You enter an interstate by an entrance ramp, paying careful attention to the signs because an exit ramp marked do not enter and wrong way often sits next to the entrance ramp, and advisory speed signs appear on ramps that curve sharply [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A04
About halfway along the entrance ramp check the interstate traffic with quick glances over your shoulder and to the side, watch the vehicles ahead of you entering the acceleration lane, use your turn signal, and look for a gap in approaching traffic while adjusting your speed to meet it [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A04
As you merge make sure you are traveling at the same speed as the other traffic, and do not cut sharply to the left into the traffic stream but follow the lane, merge, and only then change lanes [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A04
If another vehicle is ahead of you in the acceleration lane be prepared for it to slow or stop without warning, and do not stop on the ramp or in the acceleration lane [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A04
If no gap in traffic is available it may be necessary to drive onto the shoulder beyond the end of the acceleration lane and stop, but because entering the traffic stream from a stop is hazardous this maneuver is a last resort [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A04
Traffic already on the interstate has the right-of-way, and you cannot count on other drivers seeing you or moving over to give you room to enter [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A05
When exiting an interstate watch for the signs that show where your exit is and which lane to use, then signal and move into that lane well before the exit, because changing lanes at the last moment risks missing the exit or causing a crash [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F25 | anchor: A05
Most interstate exits have a deceleration lane for slowing before the exit ramp, so never slow down on the interstate itself but wait until you are in the deceleration lane and brake gently until your speed matches the posted exit ramp limit [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F26 | anchor: A05
Interstate shoulders are only for disabled vehicles and must not be used for changing drivers, reading a map or other non-emergency purposes, which belong in a rest area or off the interstate [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F27 | anchor: A05
Do not stop in an exit gore, the triangular area between the through lane and the exit ramp, because a driver who missed the exit may try to cross the gore and strike your vehicle [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F28 | anchor: A05
No parking is permitted on the shoulders of interstates, and parked vehicles may be towed [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F29 | anchor: A05
Never drive faster than the legal speed limit, do not drive slower than fifty-five miles per hour on an interstate unless weather or road conditions are bad or a lower speed is posted, and always drive at a steady speed [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F30 | anchor: A05
Driving much slower than other interstate drivers creates a hazard because others may be forced to change lanes abruptly, so always drive in the right-hand lane unless you are passing another vehicle [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F31 | anchor: A05
State law requires headlights to be turned on during adverse conditions, and in such conditions you should adjust your driving, keep an adequate following distance and adjust your speed to allow a safe stop [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0069]

items.why: Route numbering, entering and exiting steps and interstate speed rules are recall items served by standard flashcards and quiz questions, so no separate practice mode is needed.

corpus_stability.reason: The West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook is a periodically revised official edition, so its accessibility and interstate-driving pages change at most with a new edition.
